title: Heber H. Hatfield dehydration plant
description: Hatfield Industries’ head office is on the left, with the Hatfield chip plant on the right. After a devastating fire in 1946 destroyed the dehydration plant, Heber Hatfield sought a new opportunity for the local potato industry. Hartland, surrounded by potato fields and farms, had long relied on supplying dehydrated potatoes for allied forces during two wars, making local farmers dependent on Hatfield for a market. During a trip south, Hatfield discovered potato chips and envisioned a new future for Hartland—potato chip production. “Golden Crisp” potato chips, manufactured by Hatfield Industries Ltd., were set to go into production in 1950.
